vocabulary.meaning_en: a situation where people understand something wrongly
vocabulary.example: I think there's been a misunderstanding about the date.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a mistake where things or people are confused (informal)
vocabulary.example: There was a mix-up with the hotel booking.
There's a note from the boss on my desk.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the goods a company has ready to sell
vocabulary.example: We need more stock for next month.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a way of controlling how many goods a company keeps
vocabulary.example: Our stock management system tells us when to order more.

vocabulary.meaning_en: how much people want to buy something
vocabulary.example: There is high demand for the new model.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to move or work as fast as something else
vocabulary.example: We must keep up with demand.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an idea you offer for someone to think about
vocabulary.example: Please write me a couple of pages of suggestions.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to think of an idea or plan
vocabulary.example: She came up with a great idea.
I left the report on your desk.
We have a new range of office chairs.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an official paper that shows you achieved something
vocabulary.example: He has a certificate for Salesman of the Year.
The window was left open overnight.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (of wind) to move things through the air
vocabulary.example: The wind blew the papers everywhere.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a very good job or result
vocabulary.example: This report is an excellent piece of work.
Tom got the credit for Anna's work.
I'm not bothered, it doesn't matter.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an opportunity to show how good you are
vocabulary.example: The project gave her a chance to shine.

fine_lines.title: misunderstanding vs mix-up
fine_lines.explanation_ar: misunderstanding تعني أن شخصًا فهم شيئًا بشكل خاطئ، وهي أكثر رسمية. mix-up تعني خلطًا بين أشياء أو أشخاص، وهي أقل رسمية.
fine_lines.explanation_en: A "misunderstanding" is when someone understands wrongly; it is more formal. A "mix-up" is when things or people get confused; it is more informal.

examples.sentence: I think there's been a misunderstanding: the meeting is on Tuesday.
There was a mix-up and I got your bag.

fine_lines.title: must have + past participle
fine_lines.explanation_ar: must + فعل للالتزام في الحاضر. must have + التصريف الثالث لاستنتاج ما حدث في الماضي على الأرجح.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Must + verb" is for duty now. "Must have + past participle" is a guess about what probably happened in the past.

examples.sentence: You must close the window at night.
The wind must have blown the note away.

expressions.phrase: I think there's been a misunderstanding.
expressions.meaning_en: a polite way to say something went wrong
expressions.example: I think there's been a misunderstanding. I ordered blue, not red.

expressions.phrase: There's been a bit of a mix-up.
expressions.meaning_en: an informal way to say things were confused
expressions.example: Sorry, there's been a bit of a mix-up with the rooms.

expressions.meaning_en: used before you give the story
expressions.example: Please don't be angry. Let me explain what happened.

expressions.meaning_en: used to say something belongs to someone else
expressions.example: Sorry, that report is not mine.

expressions.meaning_en: used when a task feels very big
expressions.example: There's so much work. Where do I begin?

expressions.phrase: Even though you weren't meant to do it.
expressions.meaning_ar: مع أنه لم يكن مطلوبًا منك فعله.
expressions.meaning_en: you did it, but it was not your job
expressions.example: Thanks for helping, even though you weren't meant to do it.

grammar.title: Present perfect: there's been (there has been)
grammar.explanation_ar: There's been = There has been. نستخدم المضارع التام للحديث عن شيء حدث للتو وله أثر الآن: There's been a misunderstanding.
grammar.explanation_en: "There's been" = "There has been". We use the present perfect for something that just happened and matters now.
examples: There's been a mix-up with the order.
There has been a change to the plan.

grammar.title: must have + past participle (guessing the past)
grammar.explanation_ar: لنستنتج سبب ما حدث في الماضي نقول: must have + التصريف الثالث. مثال: The wind must have blown it.
grammar.explanation_en: To guess the reason for something in the past, use "must have + past participle": "The wind must have blown it."
examples: Tom must have left the window open.
The note must have fallen off my desk.

questions.question: Which phrase politely says something went wrong?
choices: I think there's been a misunderstanding.
questions.explanation_ar: هذه العبارة مهذبة لشرح وجود خطأ.
questions.explanation_en: This phrase politely says there is a mistake.

questions.question: Complete: There's been a bit of a ___.
"There's been" means...
questions.explanation_ar: There's been اختصار لـ There has been (المضارع التام).

questions.question: Complete: Let me ___ what happened.
questions.explanation_ar: بعد Let me يأتي الفعل الأساسي.
questions.explanation_en: After "Let me" use the base verb.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
choices: The wind must have blow the note.
The wind must have blown the note.
The wind must has blown the note.
The wind must blown the note.

questions.question: What does "demand" mean here: "We can keep up with demand"?
choices: how much people want to buy
questions.explanation_en: "Demand" is how much people want to buy.

questions.question: Who got the credit for Anna's work at first?
questions.explanation_ar: ظن المدير أن توم كتب التقرير.
questions.explanation_en: Paul first thought Tom wrote the report.

questions.question: "I'm not bothered" means...
questions.explanation_en: It means I don't mind / I'm not upset.
